nodes.name: Customer ID Looks Valid?
nodes.notes: Cheap format check before hitting the database. Catches copy-paste mistakes (pasting the business name, a phone_number_id, or nothing) early with a clear error instead of a confusing downstream failure.

nodes.name: Validate Source Fields
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Since the form always shows all 4 source-specific fields regardless of which Source Type is picked (Form Trigger has no conditional field visibility, see the note on KB Upload Form), this confirms the field the chosen Source Type actually needs was filled in, before wasting a Postgres lookup or, worse, silently ingesting an empty document.

nodes.name: Source Fields Valid?
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. True branch continues to the customer lookup. False branch responds with the specific reason from Validate Source Fields, so a mistake (e.g. picking 'Website page' but leaving Page URL blank) gets a clear, actionable error instead of a confusing downstream failure or a silently empty ingest.

parameters.responseBody: That doesn't look like a valid Customer ID (should be a UUID from the customers table, e.g. 8 hyphen-separated groups). Nothing was ingested. Copy the id from Supabase and try again.

parameters.query: SELECT id, business_name FROM customers WHERE id = $1::uuid

nodes.name: Load Customer
nodes.notes: Confirms the customer actually exists before writing anything into Qdrant under their name. Same service-role credential the WhatsApp agent workflow uses, reused here rather than duplicated as a second credential entry.

nodes.name: Customer Found?
nodes.notes: Never create a Qdrant collection for a customer_id that doesn't exist in Supabase. Stops silent typos from quietly building an orphaned knowledge base nothing will ever query.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ 'No customer found with id ' + $('Normalize Ingest Trigger').item.json['Customer ID'] + '. Check the id in Supabase (select id, business_name from customers) and try again. Nothing was ingested.' }}

nodes.name: Chunk Document
nodes.notes: Simple fixed-size character chunking with overlap, matching the granularity Qdrant retrieval expects (short passages, not whole documents). Each chunk is prefixed with the document title so retrieval keeps that context even mid-document. One input item (the form submission) becomes N output items (one per chunk), each embedded and upserted separately below.

nodes.name: Is Paste Text?
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. First of a chain of IF nodes routing by Source Type, deliberately chosen over a single Switch node: the Switch node's output-to-connection indexing convention wasn't verifiable with confidence, and getting it wrong would silently misroute every submission. IF's true/false contract is unambiguous and already used correctly throughout both workflows. True branch: content is already plain text, skip straight to Chunk Document. False branch: check the next source type.

nodes.name: Is File Upload?
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. False branch here means Source Type must be 'Google Sheet' (Validate Source Fields already confirmed it's one of the 4 recognized types), so no further check is needed, the false branch goes straight to the Google Sheets read node.

nodes.name: Resolve Content (Paste)
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Trivial pass-through, kept as its own node so every branch produces the same resolvedContent field for Merge Content Sources below, same pattern as the WhatsApp workflow's Resolve Message Text (Text)/(Media) split.

nodes.name: Fetch Webpage
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Fetches exactly the one URL entered, no crawling of other pages on the domain, confirmed with the user 2026-08-13 as the intended scope. neverError is set so a 404/500 response body still reaches the next node as data rather than throwing, letting Webpage Fetch OK? give a clear error instead of a generic HTTP failure. Does not render JavaScript, static HTML only, a page whose content loads via client-side JS will return an empty or near-empty body, a known limitation, not fixed here.

nodes.name: Webpage Fetch OK?
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Catches a wrong/dead URL with a clear error instead of trying to extract HTML from an error page's body and silently ingesting a 404 page's text as if it were real content.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ 'Nothing was ingested: could not fetch ' + $('Normalize Ingest Trigger').item.json['Page URL'] + ' (HTTP ' + $json.statusCode + '). Check the URL and try again.' }}

nodes.name: Extract Webpage Text
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Pulls all visible text from <body> via a CSS selector, not the full HTML markup. Simple and reliable for typical business pages (pricing, FAQ, about); pages with heavy nav/footer boilerplate will carry that boilerplate into the chunk too, a known tradeoff for staying simple, revisit with a more targeted selector per customer if retrieval quality suffers.

nodes.name: Is PDF?
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. True: already a PDF, extract text directly. False: must be .docx (the form's File field only accepts .pdf,.docx), convert to PDF first via CloudConvert, then extract.

nodes.name: Extract PDF Text
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. n8n's built-in Extract From File node, PDF operation. Output lands in $json.text.

nodes.name: Convert DOCX to PDF (CloudConvert)
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13, confirmed with the user 2026-08-13: n8n's built-in Extract From File node does not support DOCX (only PDF, CSV, HTML, JSON, ICS, ODS, RTF, text, XLS, XLSX are documented), so DOCX is converted to PDF via CloudConvert's synchronous jobs API first, then extracted the same way as a native PDF upload. Uses the synchronous endpoint (sync.api.cloudconvert.com) so the converted file's download URL comes back in this same call, no separate polling/webhook step. REQUIRES a CloudConvert account and API key (Header Auth, Authorization: Bearer <key>), a new external dependency and cost per conversion, this was a deliberate tradeoff the user chose over leaving DOCX unsupported.

nodes.name: Download Converted PDF
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. CloudConvert's synchronous job response includes the export task's result with a download URL for the converted PDF; this fetches the actual PDF bytes so Extract PDF Text (DOCX Path) can read them, same as the direct-PDF-upload path.

nodes.name: Extract PDF Text (DOCX Path)
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Same extraction operation as Extract PDF Text, applied to the CloudConvert-converted file instead of a directly uploaded PDF.

nodes.name: Resolve Content (File)
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Single convergence point for both the direct-PDF and converted-from-DOCX paths, both of which land the extracted text in $json.text via Extract From File.

nodes.name: Resolve Content (Sheet)
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Flattens every row into one text line per row (column: value pairs), joined into a single document, then chunked exactly like any other source. A very large sheet (hundreds of rows) will still get split into multiple chunks downstream by Chunk Document, each chunk covering a contiguous block of rows, retrieval quality for 'what's the price of X' style questions depends on X's row landing inside a single chunk, works well for typical small business catalogs, may need a smarter per-row-chunk strategy later for very large sheets.

nodes.name: Merge Content Sources
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13. Single convergence point for all 4 source branches. See in-code comment for why this is a Code node checking isExecuted rather than an n8n Merge node.

nodes.name: Delete Existing Chunks for This Title
nodes.notes: Added 2026-08-13 after an audit found re-ingesting the same document title created duplicate chunks in Qdrant rather than replacing them, since n8n's LangChain Qdrant node doesn't expose custom point IDs or a delete mode, upserting can't overwrite by itself. Runs once, before Chunk Document fans the submission out into N chunk items (deliberately placed here rather than after chunking, to avoid firing the same delete call N times). Calls Qdrant's REST API directly (POST /collections/{name}/points/delete with a payload filter on title). REQUIRES: (1) replacing YOUR_QDRANT_HOST in the URL with the actual Qdrant instance host (same one the Qdrant Vector Store credential below points at), and (2) a separate Header Auth credential carrying the Qdrant API key (header name typically 'api-key'), since n8n's QdrantApi credential type isn't usable by a plain HTTP Request node. ignoreHttpStatusErrors is set because a fresh customer's collection may not exist yet on first ingest, a 404 here is expected and harmless, not a real failure. FIXED 2026-08-23: host placeholder replaced with http://voxitron-qdrant:6333 (internal Docker network, no TLS). Also added the actual neverError option under options.response.response -- this note previously claimed ignoreHttpStatusErrors was set but the node's options object was empty, so a fresh customer's first-ever ingest (collection doesn't exist yet) would 404 and halt the whole execution instead of continuing past it. Credential still needs manual verification -- see chat.

nodes.name: Upsert to Qdrant
nodes.notes: Same collection naming convention the WhatsApp agent workflow reads from: kb_<customers.id>. Qdrant auto-creates the collection on first insert if it doesn't exist yet, so no separate 'create collection' step is needed for a brand new customer.

nodes.name: Embeddings OpenAI
nodes.notes: Same embedding model as the WhatsApp agent workflow's Qdrant search (text-embedding-ada-002). Must match: embeddings written with a different model than the one used at query time would not be comparable.

nodes.name: Aggregate Chunk Results
nodes.notes: Replaced a broken/invalid Aggregate config with a plain reduce-to-one-item Code node -- nothing downstream reads this node's content, only its item count matters.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ 'Ingested "' + $('Normalize Ingest Trigger').item.json['Document title'] + '" for ' + $('Load Customer').item.json.business_name + ' (' + $('Chunk Document').all().length + ' chunk(s)). Their WhatsApp agent can now answer from it.' }}

nodes.name: Default Data Loader
nodes.notes: ADDED 2026-08-23: Upsert to Qdrant's required 'Document' input had nothing connected to it -- this node was missing from the original file entirely. Reads the pre-chunked 'text' field Chunk Document already builds. Uses default Simple text splitting (chunk size 1000/overlap 200), which may re-split Chunk Document's carefully boundary-aware ~1200-char chunks slightly further -- a minor quality tradeoff, not a functional bug. Tighten later with a custom Text Splitter sized above 1200 if exact chunk boundaries matter.

nodes.name: KB Ingest Webhook
nodes.notes: ADDED 2026-08-23: frontend entry point, separate from KB Upload Form. Plain JSON POST, header-auth protected -- you must create a real Header Auth credential in n8n and share the secret with the backend, this placeholder will not work until you do. Expected body: customerId, documentTitle, sourceType (paste/website/file/sheet), content, pageUrl, fileUrl, googleSheetUrl. File uploads go through Supabase Storage first -- fileUrl, not raw file bytes -- see Normalize Ingest Trigger and Download File From URL for why.

nodes.name: Came From Webhook?
nodes.notes: ADDED 2026-08-23: form submissions already have $binary.File attached, webhook submissions only have a fileUrl and need it downloaded first.

nodes.name: Download File From URL
nodes.notes: ADDED 2026-08-23: downloads the file the frontend already uploaded to Supabase Storage, into $binary.File -- same shape KB Upload Form already produces directly, so Is PDF? / Extract PDF Text / Convert DOCX all work unchanged. The Storage object's filename must keep its real extension (.pdf/.docx) or Is PDF? can't tell them apart.

nodes.name: Delete Document (Standalone)
nodes.notes: ADDED 2026-08-23: standalone deletion, separate from Delete Existing Chunks for This Title (which only runs as a pre-step before re-ingest). Same Qdrant filter-delete call, kept as its own node so this doesn't touch that already-working node's wiring. Credential needs the same manual verification flagged earlier -- untested either way.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ 'Deleted "' + $('Normalize Ingest Trigger').item.json['Document title'] + '" for ' + $('Load Customer').item.json.business_name + ' from the knowledge base.' }}

nodes.name: Is Webhook Triggered?
nodes.notes: ADDED 2026-08-23: only the webhook path (frontend) gets async job tracking. KB Upload Form keeps its existing synchronous behavior -- an internal/manual form benefits more from an immediate result than a job id to go poll.

Processing continues in the background after this; the frontend polls kb_ingest_jobs using jobId for the real outcome, same pattern as Acknowledge Immediately in voxitron-whatsapp-agent.
